correctness.rationale: At x=0 the positive-fitness type-II map has defector fitness 1, so its first row in coordinates (x,n) is (S(n),0). Multiplying the triangular Jacobians gives the stated product for every resident period. Factoring g(g(n))−n by the fixed-point factors for g(n)=An(1−n) gives the two-cycle quadratic with roots (A+1±sqrt((A−3)(A+1)))/(2A); the two resource derivatives multiply to 4+2A−A². The affine payoff gives the variance correction by the product-of-sum-and-difference identity. In the witness A=16/5, the two payoffs are m±sqrt(21)/16, making the product m²−21/256; this is below one with mean above one exactly on the claimed open interval. The longitudinal multiplier is 4/25, and at m=403/400 the transverse multiplier is 37321/40000. The square is preserved because the resource update is nonnegative with maximum at most 4761/5120, and both fitnesses are positive. Strict contraction follows from the return Jacobian; for the reverse inequality the continuous factor x_return/x exceeds one locally on the interior side of the boundary. The equality case is not decided. The distinction from the arithmetic mean is a general nonidentity, not a claim of strict inequality for constant payoffs. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; these are analytical checks.

value.rationale: Correcting a published mean-resource heuristic with a physical stable counterexample is a worthwhile problem. The exact criterion and that counterexample mechanism are already covered. The surviving differences are scalar period-product bookkeeping and a sharp interval on an alternate parameter slice, with no independent motivation for that slice. Neither supplies a distinct valuable result as submitted.
